subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: For Darwin gateway exec, should matched allowlist commands with shell-shaped text such as `~`, pipelines, and shell wrappers auto-execute only after OpenClaw can render an enforced command, or should those shapes always require explicit approval and be documented as a limitation?
rationale: This is a command-execution security boundary: restoring the documented automation for common shell forms improves production usability, but allowing raw shell text without a rendered plan can execute something broader than the allowlist-resolved target.

options.title: Fix Enforceable Darwin Forms
options.body: Repair narrow cases such as shell-free tilde expansion or simple independently allowlisted segments while preserving prompts for command shapes OpenClaw cannot safely render.

options.title: Document The Limitation
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed prompt behavior and update docs plus warning text so operators know shell-shaped Darwin commands require explicit approval or argv-clean wrappers.

options.title: Allow Raw Matched Shell Text
options.body: Let matched Darwin allowlist commands run even without an enforced plan, accepting a broader shell-resolution security risk.

recommendation.title: Fix Enforceable Darwin Forms
recommendation.body: Repair narrow cases such as shell-free tilde expansion or simple independently allowlisted segments while preserving prompts for command shapes OpenClaw cannot safely render.

likelyOwner.reason: The current gate and recent approval-regression history are strongest around Vincent Koc's exec approval work.
